comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Fixed in e068dd65. str[] renders 'strs' and *str renders '[strs...]' again, including for rad's own commands. The placeholder is now a setter only rad's own flags call (--color, --reply, --reply-na), so no script arg can override its type name. 173d75e7 then deleted the four unreachable CreateFlag branches where half the duplicated placeholder spellings lived. One loose end split out to its own card: *int still renders 'ints' rather than '[ints...]'.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`--help` renders every list arg's value placeholder as `string,string`:

```
      --targets string,string
      --paths string,string   Paths of Rad scripts to format.
```

It used to read `strs`, and `[strs...]` for a variadic - which also told the
reader the arg was variadic. Both spellings are gone, and this reaches rad's
own commands too, not just script args.

It came in with the non-interactive prompts work (24919cca), which added this
to `StringListRadArg.Register`:

```go
// Only when the caller supplied one: script-declared list args leave this
// empty and should keep rendering as the generic "strs".
if f.ArgUsage != "" {
    arg = arg.SetCustomUsageType(f.ArgUsage)
}
```

The comment states the intent plainly, but every script-arg call site passes
the literal `"string,string"` for `argUsage` (`core/args.go:1090` and `:1132`),
so the guard is never false and the generic rendering never survives. The
snapshot churn was accepted at the time, so the flip reads as deliberate in
the diff rather than as a slip.

Independent evidence that `strs` was still the expected rendering: the
constraint-enforcement work (e5f9204a) was written on a tree without this
change, and its snapshots expected `strs` and `[strs...]` throughout. They
were regenerated to `string,string` when the two branches were combined, so
the new constraint snapshots now bless the same behavior.

Worth settling which rendering we actually want before changing anything -
`string,string` does hint at repeatability in a way `strs` doesn't, so this
may be the better output arrived at by accident. But whichever wins, the
variadic `[strs...]` form carried information that is now lost, and the code
and its comment currently disagree about what is supposed to happen.
title: List args render as `string,string` in --help, losing `strs` and `[strs...]`
